newsitem.title: USA: Procter to buy Tambrands for $1.85 biollion.
newsitem.headline: Procter to buy Tambrands for $1.85 biollion.

text.p: U.S. Consumer products company Procter & Gamble Co. said on Wednesday it will acquire Tambrands Inc. and its Tampax tampon brand for $1.85 billion.
Procter & Gamble, which makes such personal care products as Pampers disposable diapers, Pantene hair care products and Oil of Olay for skin care, said it bid $50 a share for Tambrands.

Tambrands, based in White Plains, N.Y., has manufactured Tampax tampons for more than 60 years and has 44 percent of the tampon market, the companies said in a news release. The company reported 1996 sales of $662 million.
Tambrands stock closed Tuesday at $46.125, up 62.5 cents, on the New York Stock Exchange. Procter & Gamble closed at $115.875, down $1.50, also on the NYSE.
Tambrands stock had been unusually active in the last few days as rumours of a possible acquisition by Procter & Gamble circulated through Wall Street.
Tambrand shares traded at $43.50 a week ago and traders at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said Tuesday trading in Tambrands options was unusually active in the last few days.
The NYSE said Tambrands declined to comment Tuesday on the activity in its stock. The exchange said it had contacted Tambrands "in view of the unusual market activity" in its stock.
Procter & Gamble spokesman Scott Stewart declined to comment on the trading activity as well, saying, "We took steps to ensure and maintain the confidentiality of these negotiations."

In its announcement Wednesday, Procter said it would aquire all aspects of Tambrands' business, including manufacturing, technical and other facilities. The transaction was subject to certain conditions, including Tambrands' shareholder approval and regulatory clearance, the company said.

"This acquisition provides a unique opportunity for P&G to enter the tampon category with an established brand," Procter & Gamble Chairman John Pepper said. "Tambrands began selling Tampax more than 60 years ago and today it's still the market leader. It is the most trusted tampon brand in the world."
He said the acquisition would allow the company to apply expertise it gained in the feminine protection business with its Always and Whisper pad brands, and apply it to a new market with Tampax.

Tambrands Chairman Edward Fogarty said, "Becoming part of P&G -- a world-class company with global marketing and distribution capabilities -- will accelerate the global growth of Tampax and enable the brand to achieve its full potential."
Near-term, Procter & Gamble said it planned to grow the Tampax business through broader retail distribution and new marketing programmes as well as geographic expansion.
Longer-term, it said it would look to improve existing products and develop new ones, using its research expertise and knowledge of consumers.

"It's too early to say if there will be layoffs," Stewart said. "There is often a duplication of businesses when two companies come together." Any Tambrands employees who were let go would receive Tambrands' enhanced package, he said.
Tampax was marketed in over 150 countries, employed 2,600 people worldwide and had 90 percent of its business in North America and Europe, it said.
Procter said it did not foresee any regulatory hurdles facing the acquisition.
"We will work with Tambrands to ensure an expedient regulatory review both here and internationally," Stewart said. "It really is a new market for us."
